newsitem.title: DUBAI: At least 1,000 dead, 40,000 injured in Iran quake.
newsitem.headline: At least 1,000 dead, 40,000 injured in Iran quake.

text.p: At least 1,000 people were killed and 40,000 injured on Saturday when a major earthquake devastated a rural area in eastern Iran, state media said.

Iranian television said 800 bodies were brought out from under rubble in villages outside the town of Qaen and 200 more were reported dead in areas near the city of Birjand in the south of Khorasan province.
Both areas were near the epicentre of the quake, which struck with a force of 7.1 on the Richter scale. It was Iran's most severe earthquake since 1990 when a quake killed more than 35,000 people.
Tehran radio said there was a dire need for medical and surgical personnel, medicine, blood, tents, food, ambulances, heavy earth-moving equipment and helicopters.
It said electricity and water supplies to the stricken villages had been cut off and water and other relief supplies were being transported to the area.

Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati appealed for international aid, saying Iran's relief agencies were "ready to receive assistance from our God-seeking compatriots and from those countries that would like to assist the earthquake victims", said a television report monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei expressed pain and sorrow and asked clergy in the stricken province to use religious endowments to help the victims.
President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, on an official visit to Tajikistan, expressed great regret and called for immediate relief to be rushed to their aid.
Tehran radio said 80 villages were levelled near Qaen, at the heart of an agricultural region known for its saffron production, and the area's remaining 70 were heavily damaged.
Officials said the injured were rushed to hospitals in five nearby towns and cities.
Thousands of people in the rural region were made homeless by the quake, which was felt across four provinces and a city 800 km (500 miles) away.

Mehdi Siadati, head of the disaster relief agency in Darmian district of Khorasan, told IRNA that teams had been rushed to stricken areas and a headquarters had been set up to manage relief operations.

Some 30 aftershocks ranging in strength from 3.5 to 5.5 on the Richter scale shook Birjand within four hours of the earthquake and more were expected, said the Geophysics Institute at the city of Mashhad, which was jolted by the first tremor.
It recorded the epicentre 370 km (230 miles) southeast of Mashhad, Iran's second largest city with a population of about two million, at 12:28 p.m. (0758 GMT).

The stricken area bordering Afghanistan and Turkmenistan is significantly less densely populated than a region near the Caspian Sea where 35,000 people were killed by quake-prone Iran's worst recorded jolt which measured 7.3 in 1990.
In February, at least 1,000 people were killed and more than 36,000 made homeless when a quake measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale hit northwest Iran.
IRNA said the latest quake caused panic as far away as the city of Kashan south of the capital Tehran, where people said they saw water in ponds spill over.
